source_text: Postquam ergo hoc effatus es, intulisti: Unde dicit etiam ipse Dominus: Ecce venit princeps mundi huius, et in me nihil invenit [n117] ; addisque de tuo: Nihil utique peccati, nec quod a nascente trahitur, nec quod a vivente additur. Ostende igitur dixisse Dominum in Evangelio, non se habere peccatum quod a nascente traheretur.
pass_a_gloss: After therefore you spoke this, you brought in: Whence the Lord himself also says: Behold, the prince of this world is coming, and he finds nothing in me; and you add from your own: Nothing, that is, of sin, neither what is drawn from one being born, nor what is added by one living. Show therefore that the Lord said in the Gospel that he did not have sin which would be drawn from one being born.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: After saying this, you added: “Hence the Lord himself also says, ‘See, the ruler of this world is coming, and he finds nothing in me’” (John 14:30). Then you add your own explanation: “Nothing, that is, of sin, either inherited at birth or added in the course of life.” Show, then, that the Lord said in the Gospel that he had no sin inherited at birth.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
